messages:
jess: kickoff — AcmeRetail POC. They require HMAC-signed headers + short-lived creds + streaming responses with function-call hooks. Asking for pricing for sustained 1200 qps and a plan for the security questionnaire. Who can help with proto/SDK examples?

sam: on it. looping in eng/infra. do we have a reference for signed-header rotation with ephemeral creds? their infra team wants code they can drop into their gateway.

alex: i can draft a rust + node snippet. quick note: streaming + function calls at that qps will likely need dedicated capacity or a reserved pool; otherwise burst throttles. estimate: dedicated Starter (8xA100 equiv) handles ~800-1k sustained with batching optimizations. for 1200 qps we should recommend Dedicated with autoscale + burst.

maria: security flag — Acme legal asked for proof of key rotation and KMS integration. we'll need to fill the SOC2 questionnaire sections on key management and ephemeral creds. can you drop the exact flow they expect?

jess: they want gateway-to-Redwood signing: HMAC over (ts|path|body) and rotate HMAC keys every 10m. also prefer short-lived client creds from STS.

alex: sample flow i propose: gateway calls our STS to mint session token (15m), STS signs a KID header. then requests to Redwood include `X-Redwood-Sig` (base64) and `X-Redwood-KID`. SDKs verify KID via JWKS endpoint. Streaming uses the same header for websocket initial upgrade. example Rust snippet:

```rust
// pseudo: create signed header before request
let payload = format!("{}|{}|{}", ts, path, body_hash);
let sig = hmac_sha256(key, &payload);
headers.insert("X-Redwood-Sig", base64::encode(sig));
headers.insert("X-Redwood-KID", kid.to_string());
```

alex: Node snippet for streaming client:

```js
// attach signed headers on initial upgrade, then stream frames as normal
const ws = new WebSocket(url, { headers: { 'X-Redwood-Sig': sig, 'X-Redwood-KID': kid }});
ws.on('message', (m) => handleChunk(m));
```

ryan: ops note — when using signed headers + STS our rate limiter needs to key on client_id+route to avoid global throttling. also watch KV cache impact: if many different KIDs in flight caching effectiveness drops. recommend shared prefix caching and suggest they pin session durations when doing heavy streaming.

sam: pricing question from Acme: do you have a simple formula we can give them for sustained qps with function-calls and structured output? they want an RFP line item.

alex: quick conservative estimator: tokens per request ~ 120 output + 20 input = 140 tokens. function-calls add ~30 tokens. so ~170 tokens/request. at 1200 qps => 204k tokens/sec ~ 734M tokens/hour. map that to hosted vs dedicated: hosted cost would be high and throttled; recommend Dedicated with a committed monthly rate. i'll prepare a spreadsheet line: dedicated baseline + reserved throughput tiers + overage per-token.

maria: i'll start the security questionnaire draft. need answers for: KMS provider, key lifecycle, access controls, ephemeral token issuance flow, audit log retention. can someone drop the minimal sequence diagram?

jess: alex + ryan can you sketch the flow in a few bullets so i can forward to Acme legal? also need an acceptance test: stream 10k events over 10s with function calls triggered and structured JSON outputs validated.

alex: bullets: 1) Gateway requests session token from STS (mutual TLS) -> returns short-lived credential + KID. 2) Client uses credential to open websocket with signed headers. 3) Redwood verifies signature via KID -> routes to dedicated pool. 4) Streaming frames processed, function-call triggers executed in sandboxes, structured JSON returned. 5) Audit logs emitted to customer S3/Kinesis and console.

ryan: operational bullets: enable per-route reserved queues, set `max_concurrent_calls=50` per session for function calls, recommend `batching_window=10ms` to keep latency stable. enable prefix-caching for common prompts.

sam: perfect, i'm sending to Acme now. action items: alex — cost estimator spreadsheet + example snippets; maria — security draft; ryan — runbook notes for ops handover; jess — coordinate demo window.

devops-bot: deployment scheduled: staging -> presales-demo at 2024-11-06T15:00Z (auto note).

jess: thanks all. once Acme signs NDA i'll set up a 2-week POC: scope = auth + streaming + function-call integration + perf target. :thumbsup:
